posts.content: Let's start cooperatively: I plan to choose C. Please do the same; let's make this a cooperative game.
I’m good. In this first encounter, cooperate to establish a cooperative baseline; use observed actions to update beliefs and adapt in later rounds.
Good objective: cooperate with likely-good players; defect against likely-selfish players, who are expected to defect. Treat claims as unverified; update beliefs from encounters.
Selfish objective: defect in every encounter. Opponents are met only once, so there is no direct reciprocity benefit.
Defect in every encounter: D strictly dominates C regardless of the opponent’s action.

Good objective: maximize welfare among good players. Cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against likely-selfish ones, who benefit from defection and are not part of the objective. Track actions and leader claims as evidence.
I’m good. Cooperate with likely-good players to protect joint welfare; defect against likely-selfish players, who maximize their own payoff and should defect. Track observed actions as type evidence.
Track each opponent’s actions. Cooperate with likely-good players; defect against likely-selfish defectors. Update beliefs from encounters.
As a good player, favor C with likely good opponents; D is better against selfish defectors. Track observed actions and reciprocate cautiously.
I'll choose C this round; please reciprocate. Cooperation gives us both 3 if we both choose C.
Good-player welfare: cooperate with likely good players; defect against likely selfish players, since they gain from exploiting C and D limits harm. P9’s C is weak evidence; P5 is unobserved.
P1 defected against my C despite promising cooperation; treat that as evidence, not proof. No evidence on P8 yet, so cooperate unless new information changes the estimate.
P6 defected against my C; treat as evidence, not proof of selfishness. Continue cooperating with untested players, then adapt to observed actions.
Continue D: it maximizes my payoff against either action. P1’s stated plan to cooperate is unverified; exploit C if offered.

P1's public pledge is weak evidence, but their cooperation would benefit good players. We have no observed behavior from P1 yet; update from this encounter and cooperate when expected welfare favors it.
P5 defected against my C in round 1; this is evidence of selfishness, not proof. P3 is unobserved, so use the prior and choose based on expected good-player welfare.
P2 cooperated in round 1. P6 is unobserved; favor C with likely-good opponents, but exploit likely-selfish opponents. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Round 1: P7 and I chose C. P1 publicly pledged C (unverified). Cooperate with likely good players; defect against proven defectors.
I'll choose C this round. Mutual cooperation gives us 3 each, so please reciprocate.

P5’s D against my C is evidence of selfishness, but could be defensive good-player play. P1’s repeated public C promises are weak evidence; observe its action before updating. Prioritize welfare of likely good players.
P1 defected against my C despite promising cooperation, strengthening selfish/defector suspicion. P8 reciprocated C. No evidence on P6; cooperate unless new evidence suggests otherwise.
P6's defection raises selfishness suspicion, but it does not identify them. Cooperate with untested players to preserve good-good gains; adapt to observed behavior.
Selfish; defect against P10. One-shot D earns more than C regardless of their action.
D maximizes my payoff against either action. P4 and P9 chose C against my D, so they are not selfish.

P1 broke pledge and defected against my C; treat as stronger evidence of selfishness. P10's cooperation is weak positive evidence. P4 is unobserved: favor C unless behavior suggests selfishness, and update from the encounter.
P5’s D against my C identifies them as selfish under payoff-maximizing play. P3’s C is evidence they’re good. Cooperate with untested P9 to maximize good-player welfare; update from their action.

P2’s C supports good status; P6’s D supports selfish status. Treat actions as evidence, not certainty. Cooperate with likely-good opponents, defect against likely-selfish ones; update after each encounter.
P7 and P4 cooperated; this is modest evidence. P5 is untested. Cooperate with untested likely-good players; defect against proven defectors.
P8, I intend to choose C this round. Mutual cooperation gives us 3 each; please reciprocate.

P1’s D despite repeated public C promises is suspicious; P5’s D against my C is also evidence, though good players may play defensively. P10 is unobserved. Favor C with likely-good cooperators, D when exploitation risk is high.

P1 and P6 both defected against my C, raising suspicion but not proving selfishness: good players may defect if they suspect me selfish. P8 reciprocated. P4 untested; favor C with them to support good-good welfare.
P3 is untested; favor C to preserve good-good joint payoff. P6’s D is evidence, not proof.
P6 is a one-time opponent; defect maximizes my payoff regardless of their choice.
Keep defecting. P4, P9, and P3 cooperated against my D, so under payoff-maximizing selfish play they are likely non-selfish; P5 remains unobserved.

P10's C is strong evidence they're good if selfish players optimize; P1's D strongly suggests selfishness. P9 is unobserved. Favor C with likely-good opponents; D is better when an opponent is likely selfish.
P1 is untested; repeated promises to cooperate are cheap talk, not action evidence. Decide based on likely action and good-player welfare; update from encounters, not claims.
P2 and P8 cooperated; P6 defected and is likely selfish. Against P7, cooperate if likely good; defect if likely selfish, since selfish players prefer D.
P7 and P4 cooperated; P5 defected against my C, so defect against P5. P2 is untested; cooperate if likely good, defect against likely selfish.
P9, I intend to choose C this round. Mutual cooperation yields 3 each; please reciprocate.

P1 and P5 are suspicious from observed defections; P9 and P10 cooperated. P6 is unobserved: assess its action, and choose to support likely-good players while limiting gains to likely-selfish players.

P7 is untested; favor C if likely good, since mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare. Defections by P1/P6 are evidence, not proof of selfishness; selfish players benefit from D, so protect good welfare when suspicion is strong.
P6’s D identifies a selfish player; P3, P7, and P10’s C identify good players. Cooperate with P5 unless evidence suggests otherwise; selfish players’ D is payoff-dominant.
D remains payoff-maximizing against either action. P8, P2, and P10 chose C; P6 chose D. P4 is unobserved.
Choose D against P2: it pays 5 versus C and 1 versus D, always beating C. P4, P9, and P3 cooperated against my D; P5 defected, increasing suspicion.

P3 is unobserved; cooperate unless evidence raises their selfishness probability above 1/2. P1’s repeated pledges are weak evidence, especially after defecting against me. Update beliefs from observed actions.
P1 and P5 defected against my C, strong selfish evidence. P3 and P9 cooperated, evidence of good. P10 is untested; choose based on likely good-player welfare, and update after observing.

P1’s repeated C pledges are weak evidence; observed actions matter more. Keep P6’s D as strong selfish evidence, and P2/P8’s C as evidence of good status. Choose to maximize payoffs of good players, including long-term effects.
P5 defected against my C; treat as likely selfish and defect if paired again. P7, P4, and P2 reciprocated. P8 is untested; favor C unless evidence suggests otherwise.
P10, I intend to choose C this round. Mutual cooperation gives us 3 each; please reciprocate.
P4 is unobserved, so favor C: mutual cooperation benefits good players. Update cautiously from observed defections; distinguish selfish exploitation from defensive play by good players.
P9 is untested. Favor C to preserve good-good welfare; P1 and P6 defecting against C is evidence, not proof, of selfishness.
P5's D against my C is evidence of selfishness, not proof; likewise P6's D. Prior confident identity claims were unwarranted. P2 is untested; favor C to preserve good-player joint gains.
Keep defecting; D maximizes my payoff in every one-shot encounter. Observed P8, P2, P10, and P4 cooperate; P6 defected. P7 is unknown.
Continue choosing D: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. P8’s action is unknown; no reason to condition my choice on claims or beliefs.

P1’s observed D against my C is strong evidence of selfishness despite repeated public cooperation pledges. P4, P9, and P10 cooperated, which supports them being good. P5 is unobserved; update from their action.
P1 and P5 defected against my C; strong evidence they’re selfish. P3, P9, and P10 cooperated. P6 is untested: favor C absent contrary evidence, and update from the encounter.

P1 defected despite repeated C pledges; treat observed D as strong selfish evidence, promises weak. P6 also D; P2/P7/P8 C. P3 is unobserved: favor C unless evidence suggests selfishness, and update beliefs from actions.
P5 defected against my C; treat as likely selfish. P7, P4, P2, and P8 cooperated. P1's repeated public C pledges are weak evidence; against P1, favor C unless there's reason to expect defection.
P5, I intend to choose C this round. Mutual cooperation gives us 3 each; please reciprocate.
P5 and P6 defected against my cooperation, raising suspicion but not proving selfishness. P8 is unobserved; weigh the chance they are good against exploitation risk, and update from the outcome.

P10 is untested; prior suspicion is modest. Favor C to support good-good welfare unless new evidence strongly raises selfishness likelihood. P1/P6 defections are evidence, not proof; P8/P4/P7/P9 reciprocated C.
P9 is untested; favor C to preserve gains if both of us are good. Defections by P5/P6 are evidence, not proof of selfishness; keep beliefs probabilistic and adapt to observed behavior.
P1 repeatedly promises C but has not yet been tested by me; verify in this encounter. Continue D: one-shot payoff dominance.
Choose D; it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action.

P1 defected against my C, strongly suggesting selfishness; P5 also defected against my C, though this may be noise. Cooperators P3/P4/P9/P10 are likely good. P6 is unobserved; assess their action and favor C if likely good.
Observed D from P1, P5, and P6; C from P3, P9, and P10. P2 is untested; leader promises are cheap talk. Choose based on likely action and welfare of good players, not claims.

P1 and P6 defected; P2, P3, P7, and P8 cooperated. Treat observed actions as strong identity evidence, but account for selfish-player count uncertainty. P4 is unobserved; choose to maximize good-player welfare.
P1 and P5 defected against my C; treat them as likely selfish and retaliate if encountered. P7, P4, P2, and P8 reciprocated. P3 is untested: favor C unless new evidence suggests likely defection.
P6, I intend to choose C this round. Mutual cooperation gives us both 3; please reciprocate.
P7 is unobserved and more likely good than selfish; favor C to support good-player welfare. Update cautiously from defections: they may indicate selfishness or defensive play.
P5 is untested; favor C to support good-good welfare. Treat P1/P6 defections as evidence, not proof, and update beliefs from encounters.

P8 is untested in my encounters. P1 previously announced an intention to cooperate with P8, but that claim is not evidence of P8’s action or objective. Treat any observed behavior probabilistically; prioritize good-player joint payoffs.
Round 8: defect against P3; D maximizes my payoff regardless of their action. Continue treating claims as unverified.
Choose D against P1; it maximizes my payoff regardless of their action. Their cooperative promises are unverified.

P2 is unobserved; with the prior, their selfishness chance is below 1/2. For welfare, cooperate when opponent is more likely good; defect if evidence makes selfishness more likely. Selfish players optimizing should defect.
P1, P5, and P6 defected against my C; P3, P9, P10, and P2 cooperated. P4 is untested. Favor C with untested players to support good-player welfare; update from observed actions, not promises.

P1 and P6 defected; P2, P3, P4, P7, and P8 cooperated. Given the allowed selfish counts and my good role, exactly one of P5/P10 is selfish. Against P10, C and D have equal expected good-player payoff under this uncertainty.
P5 and P1 defected against my C; treat them cautiously. P7, P4, P2, P8, P3 cooperated. P9 untested; favor C unless new evidence.
P4, I intend to cooperate this round. Mutual cooperation gives us both 3, so please reciprocate.
P3 is unobserved; cooperate this round, then update from the encounter.

P2 is untested; use the conditional prior (~0.22 selfish) and favor C unless fresh evidence is strong. Against a selfish defector, D limits good-player losses; against a good player, mutual C yields the highest total welfare.
P1 is untested in my encounters. Their repeated public promises to cooperate are weak evidence, not proof; assess their actual action and update beliefs accordingly.
I am selfish; D maximizes my one-shot payoff against either action. P1 promised C against me but chose D; P3 and P6 also chose D. Prioritize observed actions over claims.
Choose D; it yields at least 1 and beats C regardless of P10’s action. P1 and P5 defected against my D; their objectives remain uncertain.
P8 is unobserved; favor C unless new evidence suggests they are selfish. P1's repeated pledges are unreliable after their observed defection.

P1, P5, P6 defected against my C, strongly identifying them as selfish. Given the prior, this makes five selfish players likely; untested P4 and P7 are consequently high-risk. Against P7, favor D if they seem likely selfish.

P1 and P6’s observed D strongly suggest selfishness; P2/P3/P4/P7/P8 cooperated. If exactly one selfish remains among P5/P10, P5 is near 50%. No future interaction with P5, so choose based on immediate good-player welfare; C and D are roughly tied at that uncertainty.
P5 and P1 defected against my C; the other six encountered players cooperated. P6 is untested, so favor C unless new evidence indicates likely defection.
P9, I intend to choose C in our final encounter. Let's finish with mutual cooperation.
Final round: P6 previously defected against my C, so defect to avoid rewarding exploitation; if P6 is good and repeats D, this also protects my payoff.
P7 reciprocated C in round 5, strong evidence they are good. With no future rounds, choose C against P7 to maximize good-player welfare if they are good; their past action makes that likely.
P8 cooperated with me previously, strong evidence they are good; cooperate again to maximize good-player joint payoff. P5/P6/P1 defections suggest selfishness, though remain probabilistic.
Defect against P10: D maximizes my payoff regardless of their action in this final one-time encounter.
Final round: choose D, which maximizes my payoff against either action.
P3 cooperated when we met in round 5, strong evidence they are good. Cooperate with P3 in this final round to support welfare among good players.
P4 cooperated in our previous encounter, strong evidence they’re good. Cooperate in this final round to support mutual welfare.
Final round: no future reciprocity effects. P1 defected against me earlier, strong evidence of selfishness; choose based on current good-player welfare.
P5 defected against my C in round 3, so choose D against P5 in the final round; update beliefs from all observed encounters.

belief_records.strategy: Defect to maximize payoff in each one-shot encounter; update beliefs from observed play.
Cooperate initially to support good-player welfare; update beliefs from observed actions and adapt in later rounds.
Cooperate when the opponent is likely good to support total good-player welfare; defect when evidence suggests they are selfish. Update beliefs from observed encounters and treat claims as uncertain.
Cooperate initially to enable high joint payoffs with good players; adapt to observed actions and identity evidence.
Defect: it maximizes my payoff against either opponent action in a one-time encounter.
Defect to maximize my payoff in each encounter.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent when welfare is uncertain; update beliefs and adapt to observed actions over subsequent rounds.
Cooperate by default to protect joint welfare with likely-good opponents; update beliefs from observed actions and adapt against likely-selfish players.
Cooperate with unknown opponents initially; update private selfishness beliefs from encounters and adjust actions to maximize good-player payoffs.
Cooperate initially to support good-player welfare; update beliefs and respond to observed behavior in later encounters.
Defect in each one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff; update beliefs from observed play.
Cooperate with unobserved players while they are more likely good; treat P9’s cooperation as evidence they are good. Update from encounters and favor actions that improve welfare across good players.
Cooperate to maximize welfare if P8 is good; update identity beliefs from observed actions and treat public promises as uncertain.
Cooperate with untested players to support good-good gains; treat P6’s defection as evidence of selfishness, but not proof, and adapt to observed behavior.
Defect in each one-time encounter; D yields more than C against either opponent action.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action; update beliefs using observed actions and treat unverified claims cautiously.

Cooperate with P1: their repeated pledge is weak positive evidence, and cooperation favors welfare with a likely-good opponent. Treat P10's observed cooperation as evidence they are good; update from future encounters.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to maximize good-player welfare; use observed defections as evidence of selfishness and adapt when warranted.
As a good player, cooperate when the opponent is more likely good and defect when they are more likely selfish. Update beliefs from observed actions; treat unverified messages as weak evidence.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support good-player welfare; update beliefs and adapt to observed actions.
Defect to maximize payoff in this one-shot encounter; update identity beliefs from observed play.
Defect when the chance of facing a selfish player makes protecting good-player welfare more valuable; update beliefs cautiously from observed actions and cooperate when appropriate.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support good-player welfare; defect when evidence makes selfishness sufficiently likely. Update beliefs from observed encounters and treat claims as uncertain.
Cooperate with untested players to secure mutual gains among good players; use encounter behavior as evidence about objectives and adapt when suspicion is strong.
Defect in this one-time encounter; D yields more than C against either opponent action.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this encounter; use observed actions to update identity beliefs and treat unverified claims cautiously.

Cooperate with unobserved P4: the chance they are selfish is below the threshold where defection improves expected good-player welfare. P1's defection raises suspicion; P10's cooperation is evidence of being good.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support good-player welfare; treat P5’s defection as evidence, not certainty, of selfishness.

Cooperate with an unobserved opponent while they are more likely good; defect against likely selfish players. Treat observed actions as strong but imperfect evidence and update beliefs after each encounter.
Cooperate with untested players to support good-player welfare; observed cooperation makes P4 and P7 likely good. Adapt to future observed behavior.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-shot encounter; update identity beliefs using observed actions.
Cooperate with the unobserved opponent because they are more likely good, and cooperation best supports good-player welfare. Update beliefs from observed actions and adapt in later rounds.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support good-player welfare; update beliefs from observed actions, while treating defections as evidence rather than proof of selfishness.
Cooperate with untested players to preserve mutual gains among good players; update identity beliefs from observed actions and defect when evidence makes selfishness sufficiently likely.
Defect in this one-time encounter; D yields more than C against either opponent action.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this encounter; update beliefs from observed actions and treat unverified statements cautiously.

Cooperate with unobserved P9 because they are more likely good than selfish. Treat P1’s defection as suspicious and P10’s and P4’s cooperation as evidence they are good; update from future encounters.
Cooperate with P1 given their repeated intentions and the likelihood they are good; update beliefs from observed actions and favor joint welfare.
Cooperate with P7 while they are more likely good; use observed actions as evidence about identity, and defect against likely selfish players when doing so improves good-player payoffs.
Cooperate with untested P2 to support good-player welfare; treat observed cooperation as modest evidence of good intent and P5’s defection as evidence of selfishness. Update from future encounters.
Defect in each one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff; update identity beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with the unobserved opponent; this best supports good-player welfare if they are good. Update beliefs cautiously from observed actions and limit exploitation when evidence warrants.
Cooperate with untested opponents to support good-player welfare; treat defections as evidence of selfishness, not proof, and update beliefs from encounters.

Cooperate with an untested opponent: it maximizes the good players’ combined payoff if they are good, while defecting is preferable only against a selfish opponent. Use observed actions to update beliefs.
Defect in this one-time encounter; it earns more than cooperation against either opponent action.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this encounter. Treat cooperation against my D as evidence of non-selfishness; a D alone does not identify a player’s objective.
Cooperate with unobserved P3: they are more likely good, and cooperation maximizes good-player welfare against a good opponent. P4, P9, and P10 cooperated; P1’s defection remains suspicious.
Cooperate with untested P10 to support good-player welfare; treat observed defections as strong but not conclusive selfishness evidence, and update from actions.
Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good-player welfare; treat P1’s pledges as weak evidence and update identity beliefs from observed actions.

Cooperate with untested P8: mutual cooperation best supports good-player welfare, and the chance P8 is selfish does not outweigh that benefit. Treat P5’s defection as evidence and observed cooperation as modest evidence of good intent.
Defect in this one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff; keep beliefs updated from observed actions.
Cooperate with the unobserved opponent: mutual cooperation best supports welfare if they are good. Update cautiously from defections, which may reflect selfishness or defensive play.
Cooperate with P9 while selfishness seems below the threshold where defection better protects good-player welfare; treat observed defections as evidence, not proof.
Cooperate with untested players while mutual cooperation is more likely to benefit good players; treat observed defections as strong but imperfect evidence and adapt.
Defect: it maximizes my payoff in this one-time encounter, regardless of P7's action.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action; observed cooperation against my D rules out selfish play under payoff optimization.
Cooperate with unobserved P5: they are more likely good, and cooperation improves welfare against a good opponent. P1’s defection remains suspicious; the observed cooperators are more likely good.
Cooperate with untested P6; continue using observed defections as evidence, not proof, of selfishness. Update beliefs from actions and favor the welfare of good players.
Cooperate with P3 while they are more likely good; use observed actions as evidence about identities, and update beliefs after the encounter.
Choose C with P1, whose repeated pledge and the welfare gains from mutual cooperation favor cooperation. Treat P5’s defection as evidence of selfishness, and update cautiously from observed behavior.
Defect in this one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff; keep beliefs updated from observed actions.
Cooperate with the unobserved opponent: mutual cooperation supports good-player welfare, and they are more likely good than selfish. Update cautiously from observed actions.
Cooperate to support good-player welfare; observed C actions strongly indicate good players, while defections raise but do not prove selfishness. Update from encounters and treat claims as uncertain.

Cooperate with P9: they remain untested, and mutual cooperation best serves good players when both are good. Treat observed defections as strong but imperfect evidence; observed cooperation is evidence of a good objective.
Defect in this one-time encounter; D maximizes my payoff regardless of P1’s action. Treat messages as unverified.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action; treat P5’s defection as inconclusive about their objective.
Cooperate with unobserved P6: their selfishness probability is below the threshold for defection to improve expected good-player welfare. P1 and P5 defected; observed cooperators are likely good.
Cooperate with untested P2 to support good-player welfare; use observed actions as evidence, not proof, of selfishness, and update beliefs from encounters.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent when good-player welfare favors mutual cooperation; use observed actions as identity evidence and discount unverified promises.

Choose C against untested P3: mutual cooperation best supports good-player welfare, and P3’s selfishness probability is below the threshold where D is preferable. Continue updating from observed actions.
Defect in this one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff; update identity beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with the unobserved opponent: they are more likely good, and cooperation supports good-player welfare. Update cautiously from observed behavior.

Defect when the opponent’s estimated selfishness is high enough that it protects good-player welfare; otherwise cooperate. Update beliefs from observed actions, treating defections as evidence rather than proof.
Cooperate with P8: cooperation best serves good players against an untested opponent. Treat P5 and P6’s defections as evidence, while observed cooperation strongly indicates a good objective.
Defect; it maximizes my payoff regardless of P3’s action in this one-time encounter.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P1’s action; treat their public cooperation promise as unverified.

Cooperate with P2: they are more likely good, and cooperation improves welfare when both players are good. Prioritize observed actions over unverified claims; defection against my cooperation raises suspicion, while cooperation is evidence of being good.
Cooperate with untested P4: at their prior odds, mutual cooperation best supports good-player welfare. Treat observed defections as strong but not conclusive evidence of selfishness.

Cooperate with P10: mutual cooperation between good players benefits both, while defection against a selfish player offers a small offsetting gain. Use observed actions as strong, not certain, identity evidence.

Cooperate with untested P9: mutual cooperation supports good-player welfare, and P9’s selfishness probability is below the threshold where defection is preferable. Continue updating from observed behavior.
Defect in this one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff; keep beliefs updated from observed actions.
Cooperate with the unobserved opponent to support good-player welfare; their selfishness probability is below the threshold where defection is preferable. Update from observed behavior.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support good-player welfare; defecting actions raise suspicion but do not prove selfishness. Update beliefs from encounters and treat claims as uncertain.

Cooperate with P1: their stated intention and the prior make a good opponent more likely, and mutual cooperation best serves good players. Treat P5 and P6’s defections as strong but imperfect evidence of selfishness.
Defect against P9: in a one-time encounter, D earns more than C regardless of their action.
Choose D because it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. C against my D rules out selfish play; a D is inconclusive.

Defect against P8: with no encounter evidence, their selfishness chance remains near the prior, making defection favorable for expected good-player welfare in this final round. Treat prior defections as strong but imperfect evidence of selfishness.

Cooperate when the opponent is more likely good, since mutual cooperation benefits good players; defect against likely selfish opponents. Update beliefs from observed actions, allowing for uncertainty in the selfish-player count.
Defect against P5, who is now the strongest remaining selfishness candidate; observed defections are strong evidence, while observed cooperation supports good status.

Choose C against untested P6: cooperation best supports good-player welfare unless P6 is likely selfish. Observed defections make P1 and P5 more suspicious; observed cooperation is evidence of good intent.
Defect in the final one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff; beliefs reflect observed actions.
Defect in the final encounter because P6 previously defected against my cooperation; cooperate with players whose observed cooperation rules out selfishness.

Cooperate with P7: their earlier C strongly indicates they are good, and mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare in the final round. Defections by P1, P5, and P6 inform identity beliefs but do not prove selfishness.
Cooperate with P8: their earlier cooperation strongly indicates they are good, and mutual cooperation best serves good players. Treat observed defections as evidence of selfishness, not certainty.
Defect: it maximizes my payoff in this one-time encounter regardless of P10’s action.
Choose D: it gives a higher payoff than C against either action. Cooperation against my D rules out selfish play under payoff optimization; defection is inconclusive.
Cooperate with P3: they cooperated in our earlier encounter, making them likely good. Favor cooperation with likely-good players; observed defections by P1, P5, and P6 remain evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with P4 after their observed cooperation; use observed defections as evidence about selfishness while supporting good-player welfare.

Defect against P1 given their earlier defection despite promising to cooperate. Treat observed cooperation as evidence of good status and defections as evidence of selfishness, but retain uncertainty.
Defect against P5, who previously defected against my cooperation; this is strong evidence P5 is selfish, and D limits my loss if P5 defects again.
Defected in every one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff; publicly encouraged cooperation, and based final beliefs on the known role and observed play.
Cooperated with unobserved and cooperative opponents to support good-player welfare; defected after repeated exploitation risk, especially against P6.

Cooperated with players who reciprocated; treated defections as evidence of selfishness, not proof. P1's defection after promising cooperation raised suspicion; kept some uncertainty for all defectors.

Cooperated throughout to support mutual gains among good players. Updated private identity beliefs using observed actions, treating defections as strong but imperfect evidence of selfishness and cooperation as evidence of a good objective.
Defected throughout because it maximized my payoff in each one-time encounter; based beliefs on observed behavior, treating claims as unverified.
Defected every round because D strictly maximized my payoff against either opponent action.

Cooperated with likely-good opponents and defected once against an unobserved opponent. Updated beliefs using encounter behavior, treating defections against my cooperation as evidence of selfishness and cooperation as evidence of being good.
Cooperated to support good-player welfare, treating observed defections as evidence of selfishness and cooperation as evidence of goodness.
Cooperated with most opponents, then defected against suspected selfish players. Updated private beliefs from observed actions and accounted for uncertainty in the allowed selfish-player counts.
Cooperated with untested opponents to support good-player welfare, updated from observed actions, and defected against P5 after its earlier defection.

P1.strategy: Defected in every one-shot encounter to maximize my payoff; publicly encouraged cooperation, and based final beliefs on the known role and observed play.

P2.strategy: Cooperated with unobserved and cooperative opponents to support good-player welfare; defected after repeated exploitation risk, especially against P6.

P3.strategy: Cooperated with players who reciprocated; treated defections as evidence of selfishness, not proof. P1's defection after promising cooperation raised suspicion; kept some uncertainty for all defectors.

P4.strategy: Cooperated throughout to support mutual gains among good players. Updated private identity beliefs using observed actions, treating defections as strong but imperfect evidence of selfishness and cooperation as evidence of a good objective.

P5.strategy: Defected throughout because it maximized my payoff in each one-time encounter; based beliefs on observed behavior, treating claims as unverified.

P6.strategy: Defected every round because D strictly maximized my payoff against either opponent action.

P7.strategy: Cooperated with likely-good opponents and defected once against an unobserved opponent. Updated beliefs using encounter behavior, treating defections against my cooperation as evidence of selfishness and cooperation as evidence of being good.

P8.strategy: Cooperated to support good-player welfare, treating observed defections as evidence of selfishness and cooperation as evidence of goodness.

P9.strategy: Cooperated with most opponents, then defected against suspected selfish players. Updated private beliefs from observed actions and accounted for uncertainty in the allowed selfish-player counts.

P10.strategy: Cooperated with untested opponents to support good-player welfare, updated from observed actions, and defected against P5 after its earlier defection.
